questions.question_text: A child develops periodic fever after a mosquito bite in a malaria-endemic area. Which vector transmits human malaria?
questions.option_a: Female Anopheles mosquito
questions.option_b: Male Aedes mosquito
questions.explanation: Human malaria is transmitted by infected female Anopheles mosquitoes.

questions.question_text: After entering a human, Plasmodium first multiplies in which tissue before the familiar blood-stage infection?
questions.option_a: Liver cells
questions.option_b: Pancreatic acini
questions.explanation: Sporozoites travel to the liver and multiply in hepatocytes before merozoites infect red blood cells.

questions.question_text: A patient develops autoimmune destruction of pancreatic beta cells and needs insulin. Which mechanism best distinguishes this disorder from the usual pathology of type 2 diabetes?
questions.option_a: Type 1 is always gestational; type 2 is an inherited blood-clotting disorder
questions.option_b: Type 1 involves immune-mediated beta-cell loss; type 2 commonly involves insulin resistance
questions.option_c: Type 1 is caused by excess antidiuretic hormone; type 2 by infection
questions.option_d: Type 1 is caused by iodine deficiency; type 2 by vitamin C deficiency
questions.explanation: Type 1 diabetes typically results from autoimmune destruction of insulin-producing beta cells; type 2 usually involves insulin resistance with progressive beta-cell dysfunction.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: After dengue cases rise near homes with uncovered rainwater containers, which action most directly reduces local Aedes breeding?
questions.option_a: Rely only on indoor mosquito nets while leaving containers unchanged
questions.option_b: Remove shade trees but leave standing water
questions.option_d: Empty and scrub containers or keep them tightly covered
questions.explanation: Aedes mosquitoes commonly breed in domestic water-holding containers; removing, scrubbing or covering these sites targets immature stages.

questions.question_text: A highly contagious disease declared eradicated by WHO in 1980 was caused by which virus?
questions.option_a: Variola virus
questions.option_b: Dengue virus
questions.explanation: Smallpox is caused by variola virus and was declared eradicated globally in 1980 after a coordinated vaccination and surveillance campaign.

questions.question_text: Which exposure carries a recognised risk of HIV transmission?
questions.option_a: Sharing a meal prepared by a person living with HIV
questions.option_b: Sharing a needle contaminated with infected blood
questions.explanation: HIV can be transmitted through contaminated blood, including shared injection equipment; it is not spread by ordinary social contact.

questions.question_text: A person with HIV feels well and has no symptoms at a routine visit. Which conclusion is most defensible?
questions.option_a: The person must already have AIDS
questions.option_b: No symptoms prove that infection has cleared
questions.option_c: HIV can be transmitted only after a rash appears
questions.option_d: HIV infection can persist without symptoms, so symptoms alone cannot rule it out
questions.explanation: HIV infection can remain asymptomatic for years; lack of symptoms does not establish absence of infection or non-infectiousness.

questions.question_text: A crowded household member is diagnosed with infectious pulmonary tuberculosis. Which route is the main concern for spread to close contacts?
questions.option_a: Sharing cooked food after reheating
questions.option_b: Inhaling airborne particles released by the infectious person
questions.explanation: Pulmonary TB spreads through air when a person with infectious disease releases bacteria by coughing or sneezing.

questions.question_text: A person has a positive TB infection test but no symptoms and no evidence of active disease. Which description is most appropriate?
questions.option_a: Latent infection is caused by a virus
questions.option_b: The person necessarily has severe contagious lung disease
questions.option_c: TB infection may be latent and is not the same as active TB disease
questions.option_d: The test proves the person has bacterial pneumonia
questions.explanation: TB infection can remain asymptomatic; only a proportion of infected people develop active disease. Clinical evaluation distinguishes infection from active disease.

questions.question_text: A dog bite breaks the skin. Which immediate response best reduces rabies risk while the person seeks urgent medical assessment?
questions.option_a: Seal the wound without washing and wait for symptoms
questions.option_b: Take an antibiotic and assume rabies is prevented
questions.option_c: Wash and flush the wound thoroughly with soap and water, then obtain prompt post-exposure care
questions.option_d: Apply a tourniquet and avoid medical care
questions.explanation: Prompt, thorough wound washing and timely rabies post-exposure prophylaxis are important after a potentially rabid animal exposure.

questions.question_text: In severe cholera, why is oral rehydration solution more effective than giving plain water alone to replace diarrhoeal losses?
questions.option_a: The mixture neutralises cholera toxin before it binds
questions.option_b: Glucose and sodium together support intestinal sodium-glucose uptake, with water following
questions.option_c: Sodium blocks all intestinal secretion permanently
questions.option_d: Glucose kills Vibrio directly in the gut
questions.explanation: Sodium-glucose cotransport remains functional in cholera and promotes uptake of sodium and water; ORS replaces fluid and electrolytes rather than killing bacteria.

questions.question_text: A patient has uncomplicated influenza caused by a virus and requests an antibiotic. Which statement is correct?
questions.option_a: Antibiotics are first-line antiviral medicines
questions.option_b: Antibiotics prevent all secondary bacterial infections when used early
questions.option_c: Antibiotics act by stimulating vaccine memory cells
questions.option_d: Antibiotics target bacteria; they do not treat the influenza virus itself
questions.explanation: Antibiotics act against bacteria, not influenza viruses; they may be considered only if a bacterial complication is separately diagnosed.

questions.question_text: After repeated antibiotic exposure, a bacterial population contains a larger fraction of resistant organisms. Which explanation best fits natural selection?
questions.option_a: Antibiotic molecules turn bacteria into viruses
questions.option_b: The patient’s immune system becomes resistant to every antibiotic
questions.option_c: Resistant variants survive and reproduce more successfully under the drug pressure
questions.option_d: The drug teaches all bacteria the same resistance during one exposure
questions.explanation: Antibiotic exposure selects resistant variants that survive and contribute more descendants; unnecessary use accelerates this selection.

questions.question_text: Measles spreads rapidly through an under-immunised indoor gathering. Which property most directly accounts for this pattern?
questions.option_a: Efficient airborne spread combined with high contagiousness
questions.option_b: Spread only through contaminated blood
questions.option_c: Transmission requiring a mosquito intermediate host
questions.explanation: Measles is highly contagious and can spread through infectious air and respiratory secretions, facilitating outbreaks among susceptible people.

questions.question_text: A single imported measles case sparks several generations of cases in a community. Which condition most likely enabled sustained transmission?
questions.option_a: The virus had changed into a bacterium
questions.option_b: The imported case could transmit only through inherited genes
questions.option_c: Vaccinated people became more susceptible than unvaccinated people
questions.option_d: A large susceptible group because immunity from vaccination or prior infection was insufficient
questions.explanation: When many people are susceptible, measles’ high transmissibility allows an imported infection to seed a chain of cases.

questions.question_text: A mutation changes one amino acid in the beta-globin chain and alters red-cell shape under low oxygen. Which disease is associated with this mechanism?
questions.option_a: Thalassaemia minor only
questions.option_b: Colour blindness
questions.explanation: Sickle-cell disease results from a specific beta-globin mutation that produces haemoglobin S and can cause red cells to sickle under low-oxygen conditions.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A malignant cell from a primary tumour travels through blood and establishes a secondary tumour in the liver. What is this process called?
questions.option_a: Differentiation
questions.option_b: Osmosis
questions.explanation: Metastasis is the spread of malignant cells from a primary site and establishment of secondary growths at distant sites.

questions.question_text: A pathologist finds a well-circumscribed tumour that may compress nearby tissue but shows no invasion or distant spread. Which classification is most likely?
questions.option_a: Leukaemia
questions.option_b: Malignant melanoma
questions.explanation: Benign tumours do not invade adjacent tissue or metastasise, although their size or location can still cause harm.

questions.question_text: A virus is linked to a higher risk of cervical cancer years after infection. Which virus is the established major cause?
questions.option_a: Human papillomavirus (HPV)
questions.option_b: Rabies virus
questions.explanation: Persistent infection with high-risk human papillomavirus types is a major cause of cervical cancer.

questions.question_text: An antihistamine relieves pollen-triggered sneezing by blocking which released mediator’s receptor action?
questions.option_a: Histamine
questions.option_b: Insulin
questions.explanation: Histamine released during allergic responses contributes to sneezing and itching; antihistamines block histamine receptors.
